official.description: The Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation provides financial assistance to provide training opportunities for students in New Zealand and the South Pacific region. It commemorates Barbara Wood MBE, Dominion President of the NZ Federation of Country Women's Institutes 1970-1974 and Deputy World President of the Associated Country Women of the World 1977-1979, who died in the Mt Erebus air disaster. The programme is administered by the New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a small, need-weighted top-up of up to NZD 1,000 a year for South Pacific-born tertiary students, so treat it as part of a wider funding package rather than a main award. Eligibility turns on where you were born, not where you now live or study, so a student born in Samoa, Tonga, Niue, Fiji, Australia or New Zealand who is enrolling anywhere in New Zealand or the wider South Pacific qualifies on that test. Because the trustees size the grant to the need and cost of your course, a cheap certificate course and an expensive nursing degree will not be treated alike. Recipients can reapply every year, so a first success is a renewable relationship rather than a one-off.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A South Pacific-born tertiary student, at any level from certificate to bachelor's, whose course fees and living costs exceed their other support.
application_readiness_checklist: Download and read the Conditions for Application first, because the Federation refuses incomplete submissions outright
Gather proof of place of birth (birth certificate or passport) before you start the form
Request your 2027 course cost breakdown and any evidence of financial need early, since the trustees weigh both
Have the completed form and every required paper physically in the Federation's hands before 1 February 2027, not merely posted on that date
common_rejection_risks: Sending the form without the full set of papers listed in the Conditions for Application, which the Federation says means the application is not accepted at all
Submitting after 1 February 2027 or assuming a late posting date is enough
Assuming the award follows a set schedule: the trustees exercise discretion, so a strong financial-need case still needs to be evidenced
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, travel, and most or all of tuition: NZD 1,000 a year is a modest contribution against a New Zealand tertiary tuition bill, so the bulk of fees, accommodation and day-to-day costs must be met from other sources.
document_audit: The Conditions for Application is a separate download from the application form, and applicants routinely submit one without the other
Place-of-birth evidence must be documentary, not a statement in the form
alerts: The 2026 round is already closed; the live round is for the 2027 academic year and closes 1 February 2027
Recipients may reapply in later years, so keep the enrolment and cost evidence from this year for a future application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Download the form and conditions, assemble the papers, and post a complete paper application to the Federation so that it arrives before the 1 February 2027 closing date.

Awards are sized by qualification level and targeted streams exist for refugee and migrant women, STEM students, trade and apprenticeship women, solo parents and Pasifika women in Early Childhood or Primary Education.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-off grant of $1,000 to $3,000 whose size is fixed entirely by the NZQCF level you are studying at, so the single biggest thing you control is how your qualification is levelled on the NZQF. The panel says plainly that it is not looking for perfect grades and instead weighs why you returned to study, where you are heading, and what the money will let you do. Because applicants can hold only one award per level of study, a certificate graduate who later enrols in a degree can apply again at the higher level. Applications for the 2026 round closed at 11.59 pm on 25 August 2026 and every applicant hears back by email in October 2026, with no next opening date published yet.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A woman returning to New Zealand tertiary study after a break, especially a refugee or migrant, a solo parent, a Pasifika woman in Early Childhood or Primary Education, or a woman entering a trade or a non-traditional field.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the NZQCF level of your 2027 qualification first, because that determines whether you are applying for $1,000, $1,500 or $3,000
Check you have not already received a Trust award at that same level, which makes you ineligible for this stream
Draft the 'why I returned to study' narrative early, since the panel weights it alongside your goals
Arrange certified copies of your 2027 enrolment and ID now, because payment depends on them
Keep an eye on the Trust's Education Awards page and newsletters from November 2026 onwards for the next window
common_rejection_risks: Assuming an old Trust award at a lower level blocks you, or that a higher-level application is allowed when you already hold that level
Applying for postgraduate study, which the FAQ explicitly rules out
Missing the hard 11.59 pm cut-off: the Trust states it does not accept late applications and simply closes the form
Writing a grades-focused application when the panel has said it values determination and completion potential over marks
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond a single $1,000-$3,000 payment: tuition for the year, living costs, transport and course materials must be met from other sources, and no travel or accommodation component is published.
document_audit: Certification matters: the Trust requires certified evidence of enrolment and identity before any money is released, so uncertified photocopies will stall payment
Check your junk folder for the outcome email, because the Trust warns the confirmation and result messages are frequently filtered
alerts: The Trust does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications, so you cannot ask why you missed out
Award values may change each year depending on funds available, so the $3,000 degree figure is not guaranteed for future rounds
You may apply for more than one Trust award simultaneously, including the Outward Bound personal growth awards
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online form only: complete and register the Trust's application form during the published window, receive a browser and email confirmation, then supply certified enrolment and ID evidence if selected.
